headline: Learned representations couple biological context with drug and perturbation prediction
label: Machine Learning Drug Prediction
summary: Recent preprints and papers pair learned representations with biological priors across drug, miRNA, and perturbation prediction tasks.
synthesis: The common thread is coupling learned molecular, cellular, or image-derived representations with biological or chemical context to predict drug interactions, drug response, or perturbation outcomes. B-SMART-Former combines ChemBERTa, Morgan fingerprints and ProtBERT in an explainable transformer for biotech-small-molecule drug-drug interactions, while MICON models chemical compounds as treatments within contrastive microscopy representation learning. Perturbation work spans a benchmark of deep and non-deep single-cell perturbation models on differential expression classification and a decomposition of Perturb-seq responses aligned to gene coessentiality. Two miRNA-disease papers use attention over similarity or association networks, and a hierarchical graph attention autoencoder with LSTM dose encoding models dose-specific olaparib resistance. What is new is the explicit use of biological structure as an alignment target, such as gene coessentiality and similarity networks, alongside built-in interpretability in M3-Gen and B-SMART-Former.
